jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Japan governs AI through a framework law and soft-law guidelines rather than binding AI-specific obligations. The 2025 AI Promotion Act, fully in force since 1 September 2025, set up the AI Strategic Headquarters under the Prime Minister, which adopted the first AI Basic Plan in December 2025 (revised July 2026) and a guideline on the appropriate research, development and use of AI; the Act has no penalties but lets the government investigate and publicise serious misuse. Practical rules come from the METI and MIC AI Guidelines for Business (now version 1.2), the Japan AI Safety Institute's evaluation and red-teaming guides, and the Digital Agency's DS-920 guideline on government procurement and use of generative AI. Data protection and copyright set the main binding limits: the Personal Information Protection Commission has warned generative AI providers and a 2026 amendment eases the use of personal data for AI development as statistics, while Copyright Act Article 30-4 permits AI training subject to the Agency for Cultural Affairs' interpretation. Sector regulators add rules for AI medical devices and automated driving and guidance for finance, defence and legal services, and Tokyo, Kobe, Osaka and other local governments have AI strategies, staff guidelines and, in Kobe's case, a binding AI ordinance.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry
Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 8 October 2026, covering laws and Cabinet decisions, ministries' AI guidelines (METI, MIC, the Digital Agency, the Japan AI Safety Institute and MEXT), privacy and intellectual property (the Personal Information Protection Commission, the Agency for Cultural Affairs, the Intellectual Property Strategy Headquarters and the Patent Office), sector regulators (the Financial Services Agency, the health ministry and medical devices agency, transport and police, defence and justice), and Tokyo, Osaka, Kobe, Kanagawa and other prefectures and major cities. Searches were made in Japanese and English. The Foreign Ministry's press pages and some defence and consumer pages could not be read automatically. Several prefecture and city generative AI guidelines (Kanagawa, Yokohama, Nagoya, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Kyoto) are no longer on their official websites and are held as pending. Pending: Japan's signature of the Council of Europe AI Convention (to be recorded in the regional layer), implementing rules for the 2026 data protection amendment, the commencement date of Kobe's AI ordinance, and AI guidance from other cities.

instruments.english_title: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technology (AI Promotion Act; Act No. 53 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Diet
instruments.current_status: Act No. 53 of 2025 (令和七年法律第五十三号), promulgated 4 June 2025 and in force from that day, except Chapter 3 (AI Basic Plan), Chapter 4 (AI Strategic Headquarters) and Supplementary Provisions Arts. 3-4, which came into force on 1 September 2025 (date fixed by Cabinet Order; confirmed by the Supplementary Provisions of the AI Strategic Headquarters Order and the e-Gov revision record). Not amended since; e-Gov status CurrentEnforced as of 8 October 2026. Abbreviated by e-Gov and the Cabinet Office as the 'AI法' (AI Act).
instruments.summary: Japan's framework Act on AI: it sets basic principles for AI R&D and use (international competitiveness, security, transparency and risk response, international cooperation), defines 'AI-related technology', and sets out the responsibilities of the State, local governments, R&D institutions, businesses using AI (which must cooperate with government measures) and citizens. It requires the State to issue guidelines consistent with international norms to ensure appropriate AI R&D and use (Art. 13) and to collect information, analyse cases where rights were infringed through improper AI use, and give guidance, advice and information to businesses (Art. 16), without penalties. It establishes the Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters in the Cabinet (headed by the Prime Minister) and requires a Cabinet-approved Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan (Art. 18).

instruments.official_title: 人工知能基本計画
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan (Japan's Second AI Basic Plan: 'Japan AI Transformation; A Stronger Nation. Greater Prosperity.')
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet (Cabinet decision on a draft prepared by the Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters)
instruments.current_status: Statutory plan under Art. 18 of the AI Promotion Act. First plan (subtitle 「信頼できるＡＩ」による「日本再起」) adopted by Cabinet decision on 23 December 2025; revised plan (第Ⅱ期, subtitle ～日本ＡＸ、より強く、より豊かに～) adopted by Cabinet decision on 14 July 2026 after a public consultation on the draft (19-23 June 2026) and approval of the draft by the AI Strategic Headquarters on 10 July 2026. The 2025 plan is kept on the Cabinet Office page as a past plan; the plan states it will be reviewed in principle annually. Cabinet Office provisional English translations exist.
instruments.summary: Japan's statutory national AI plan under the AI Promotion Act, setting the basic policy and the measures the government will take comprehensively, organised in four pillars: accelerating AI use, strategically strengthening AI development capability, leading AI governance, and continuous transformation toward an AI society. The July 2026 revision responds to agentic and physical AI, prioritises domain-specific 'vertical AI' and 'physical AI', calls for open 'AI sovereignty', government-wide AI use (Government AI 'GENAI'), strengthening the AI Safety Institute (frontier-model evaluation, incident and vulnerability sharing) and cyber defence. Implementation is led by the AI Strategic Headquarters with follow-up, benchmarks and in-principle annual review.

instruments.official_title: デジタル社会推進標準ガイドライン DS-920 行政の進化と革新のための生成AIの調達・利活用に係るガイドライン
instruments.english_title: Digital Society Promotion Standard Guideline DS-920: Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI for the sake of Evolution and Innovation of Public Administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Executive Committee of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society (デジタル社会推進会議幹事会); published by the Digital Agency
instruments.current_status: Normative (rules to be complied with for government information systems). First decided 27 May 2025; revised 12 June 2026, with the revision in force from 1 September 2026 (CAIO measures under 6.2 to be set by 30 June 2026; the AI-governance framework for the expanded scope of generative AI applies from 1 July 2026). Replaces the 'ChatGPT等の生成AIの業務利用に関する申合せ（第2.1版）', which it states is abolished. English provisional translation published by the Digital Agency.
instruments.scope: Japan; national government ministries and agencies (government information systems that incorporate generative AI)
instruments.summary: Standard guideline decided by the Executive Committee of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society that sets the government's generative-AI governance and the rules ministries must follow when planning, procuring, developing, providing and using generative-AI systems in government information systems (excluding systems handling specially designated secrets and similar classified information). It requires each ministry to appoint a Chief AI Officer (CAIO), report high-risk uses to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board, apply a high-risk assessment checklist, and use procurement and contract checksheets covering security, data handling, IP and output control. The 2026 revision reflects the AI Basic Plan and the AI appropriateness guideline, widens the scope of generative AI and adds provisions on AI agents, logging, terms of use and system audit.

It allows the Headquarters to set up expert panels (専門調査会) by resolution, with part-time members appointed by the Prime Minister, and leaves other operating rules to the Headquarters' chief (the Prime Minister). On this basis the Headquarters decided on 12 September 2025 to establish the Expert Panel on AI Strategy and to convene the inter-ministerial Council for the Promotion of AI Strategy.

Not revised as of 8 October 2026. The Cabinet Office page also lists the ministries' AI guidelines and international norms aligned with it. Provisional English translation published 16 January 2026.
instruments.summary: The guideline required by Article 13 of the AI Promotion Act, aligned with international norms (Hiroshima AI Process, OECD), which encourages voluntary action rather than setting a single standard of 'appropriateness'. It sets out what R&D institutions and businesses should especially do (AI governance, transparency towards stakeholders, safety, business continuity, care for data rights holders), what national and local governments should do (lead in using AI, literacy, AI governance, accountability as administrators), and what citizens should do (responsible use based on human-centric principles and AI literacy). Stakeholders are expected to respond at a level suited to their scale, role and the risks of their AI.

instruments.summary: Japan's founding AI ethics principles, drafted by the Council for Social Principles of Human-centric AI, setting out the basic philosophy (dignity, diversity and inclusion, sustainability) for an 'AI-Ready Society' under Society 5.0. It lays down seven social principles for AI: human-centricity, education/literacy, privacy protection, ensuring security, fair competition, fairness, accountability and transparency, and innovation, and calls for AI R&D and utilisation principles to be developed by developers and operators. It is non-binding and was offered to G7 and OECD discussions.

instruments.summary: Japan's first comprehensive national AI strategy, setting four strategic goals (human resources, industrial competitiveness, a sustainable society, and leadership in international AI research and networks) and concrete targets. Measures covered education reform (AI literacy for all students), restructuring the R&D system, social implementation in health, agriculture, infrastructure and mobility, data infrastructure, digital government and ethics, with the Social Principles of Human-Centric AI as its ethical basis.

instruments.summary: Policy report recommending prompt legislation on AI that balances innovation with risk response by combining laws and guidelines. It proposed a strengthened government command centre, a national AI strategy (basic plan), government guidelines aligned with the Hiroshima AI Process, and State investigation, information-gathering and guidance to businesses, plus appropriate government procurement and use of AI. These elements became the core of the AI Promotion Act.

It requires data use to promote AI, IoT and cloud technologies (Art. 3(8)) and the State to promote R&D and demonstration of AI and other advanced technologies (Art. 16). It sets programmatic duties for the State, local governments and businesses rather than obligations with penalties.

It also lets METI designate high-speed information processing semiconductors and have the IPA support their stable production through investment and guarantees. It binds government finance and support schemes rather than AI developers or users.

instruments.summary: Voluntary code agreed by the G7 under the Hiroshima AI Process, asking organisations that develop the most advanced AI systems (including frontier foundation models and generative AI) to follow, on a risk-based basis, actions such as identifying and mitigating risks across the lifecycle, post-deployment monitoring, public transparency reports on capabilities and limits, incident information sharing, AI governance and security controls, content authentication/provenance, and respect for human rights. It is part of the Hiroshima AI Process Comprehensive Policy Framework and is the reference for the OECD's Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework.

Version 1.2 adds definitions, benefits, risks and points of attention for AI agents, agentic AI and physical AI, revises the risk descriptions and the roles of each actor, clarifies terms such as training, inference and data, and reflects the AI Promotion Act and the December 2025 AI appropriateness guideline. The appendix gives practical approaches, a checklist and worksheet for implementing AI governance.

The earlier 文章生成AI利活用ガイドライン (Version 1.0 August 2023; Version 2.0 April 2024) is no longer hosted: its former URL now serves the 2026 AI Introduction and Utilization Guideline (see leads).
instruments.summary: Staff handbook telling TMG employees how to use generative AI safely in daily work, based on the Tokyo AI Strategy and the AI Introduction and Utilization Guideline. Staff must use only the bureau's secured common tools or externally approved services; using unauthorised generative AI or private devices for work breaches the TMG cybersecurity policy and can lead to disciplinary action. It sets checkpoints on confidential and personal information (common platform cleared for information up to confidentiality class A), copyright checks of prompts and outputs, and fact-checking.

instruments.english_title: Ordinance on the Utilization of AI in Kobe City
instruments.issuing_authority: Kobe City (ordinance No. 25 of March 2024, passed by the Kobe City Assembly)
instruments.current_status: Ordinance No. 25, dated 29 March 2024. Supplementary provisions: commencement on a date set by city rule within six months of promulgation (Art. 9 applies to contracts concluded on or after 1 April 2025). The city's page states the ordinance and its basic policy are in operation (22 risk assessments carried out as of 1 May 2026); the exact commencement date set by rule was not found on the city site.
instruments.summary: Municipal ordinance (11 articles) that sets basic principles for Kobe's use of AI (human dignity, safety and privacy, fairness and transparency, security, accountability) and requires the city to adopt and publish a basic AI policy. Before using AI for administrative dispositions, public-comment policy drafts and other matters with serious impact on residents, the city must assess the risk to residents' rights and interests (Art. 6). The mayor must prevent staff from entering non-disclosable information into generative AI not designated as safe (Art. 7), executives may not rely on generative AI when explaining to the assembly, and contractors need city consent to use AI in delegated dispositions or to input such information (Art. 9).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Kobe municipal AI governance instrument in Japan.

instruments.issuing_authority: Kobe City
instruments.current_status: First version made 21 June 2023; revised to v1.1 on 1 February 2024 and v1.2 on 27 September 2024. Version 1.2 is the version linked from the city's generative AI page as of 8 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Guideline explaining what Kobe City staff must observe when using ChatGPT and other generative AI at work, applying to the bureaus within the scope of the city information security standards (and the whole education board for ordinance purposes). Under the information security policy all generative AI use and system building requires review and approval by the information security administrator, and under Art. 7 of the AI ordinance information exempt from disclosure under the city's information disclosure ordinance may be entered only into generative AI designated by the mayor (none designated at v1.2; Microsoft Copilot is cleared for non-confidential information only). Staff must take training and check outputs for legal compliance, rights infringement and accuracy.

instruments.english_title: Osaka City Generative AI Usage Guideline (Version 2.4)
instruments.issuing_authority: Osaka City, Digital Integration Office (大阪市デジタル統括室)
instruments.current_status: Made 26 March 2024 (v1.0); revised 12 June 2024 (v1.1), 1 November 2024 (v2.0), 25 March 2025, 2 June 2025, 31 October 2025 and 22 December 2025 (v2.4, cover date 2025.12.22). Listed as a 指針 on the Digital Integration Office's page of rules (updated 1 April 2026).
instruments.summary: Rules for Osaka City staff on using generative AI, applying to the bureaus covered by the city's information-system and DX regulations. Common rules limit use to staff work purposes and in principle bar direct services to residents or businesses without the Digital Integration Office director's approval, prohibit consumer generative AI services usable on click-through terms (e.g. ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot), restrict AI search engines to search only, and require staff to check outputs for accuracy, bias and rights infringement, edit them, and disclose AI generation when outputs are used unedited. Later versions add rules for image, video and audio generation, contracted generative AI services and AI built into devices, and the city's AI assistant (Oasis) and RAG environments.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Osaka City municipal AI governance instrument in Japan.

In principle a special specification (生成AI利用に関する特記仕様書) is attached to contracts and agreements, and contractors must obtain the commissioning department's prior confirmation, on a set form, of the work, users, information security arrangements and their pledge to follow the usage rules; version 1.1 adds specific conditions for image and video generation because of copyright risk.

instruments.summary: Internal rules (要綱) establishing, under Art. 174(1) of the Local Autonomy Act, a specialist commissioner titled AI Governance Advisor for Osaka City. The advisor, appointed by the mayor for up to one year from experts in AI use, management and control, investigates and advises on the city's AI usage policy, the design and evaluation of AI measures and AI skills development, excluding procurement specification and evaluation work, and is bound by confidentiality.

instruments.official_title: 生成AIの調達・利活用に係るガイドライン
instruments.english_title: Aichi Prefecture Guideline on the Procurement and Use of Generative AI
instruments.issuing_authority: Aichi Prefecture (Digital Strategy Division, General Affairs Bureau)
instruments.current_status: Made 1 April 2026 (策定日 2026年4月1日); replaces, as the prefecture's guidance, the 'Guideline on the Use of Generative AI' of November 2023, which is no longer posted. Annexes: high-risk assessment sheet, generative AI system usage rules, risk-case report form.
instruments.summary: Prefectural guideline, modelled on the national DS-920 approach, that sets AI governance for procuring and using generative AI in Aichi's governor's departments, public enterprises, administrative commissions, board of education and assembly secretariat (excluding police and teachers). The Digital Strategy Director acts as Chief AI Officer: planners must submit each new generative AI system with a high-risk assessment sheet, high-risk systems are referred to a Generative AI Procurement and Utilization Promotion Council for advice before procurement, and services must log inputs and outputs and not train on inputs. Planners must monitor quality, bias, misuse and privacy after launch, and staff users must follow the separate generative AI system usage rules (Annex 2).

instruments.english_title: Hyogo Prefecture Generative AI Usage Guideline (Version 2.4)
instruments.issuing_authority: Hyogo Prefecture (Digital Strategy Division)
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 issued 19 October 2023; revised 18 December 2023 (1.1), 1 May 2024 (2.0), 22 October 2024 (2.1), 1 June 2025 (2.2), 1 April 2026 (2.3, following amendment of the prefectural information security measures guideline) and 1 September 2026 (2.4, image generation). Version 2.4 is posted on the Digital Strategy Division page with Q&A (v2.6) and prompt (v1.3) appendices.
instruments.summary: Guideline made under Art. 43(5) of the Hyogo Information Security Measures Guideline that sets rules for all prefectural staff using text, image and audio generative AI systems. Microsoft Copilot on the prefectural network and approved paid services may be used; other services require prior approval from the head of division recorded in a permission register. Staff may not input information classed confidentiality 2 or higher or personal information, must check and edit outputs and label unedited AI output as AI-generated, check intellectual property, and contractors must be required by contract to follow the guideline.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Hyogo Prefecture prefectural AI governance instrument in Japan.

instruments.summary: Guideline setting what staff of the governor's departments, administrative commissions (except the public safety commission), assembly secretariat and public enterprises must observe when using generative AI within the Chiba information security policy; school education is excluded. Only services designated by the Digital Reform Promotion Bureau may be used (others need prior application and designation), with an annex fixing for each service the users, permitted business and information that may be input. Staff must take designated training, may not enter work information into AI installed privately on personal devices, must keep personal information to the minimum, check and edit outputs, include generative AI terms in contracts where deliverables contain AI output, and report AI-specific risk incidents on a set form.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Chiba Prefecture prefectural AI governance instrument in Japan.

instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated 1 November 2023, the date city-wide operation began. Still the version posted on the city's page as of 8 October 2026; no later version found.
instruments.summary: Guideline setting rules for introducing click-through (terms-of-service) cloud generative AI such as ChatGPT in Chiba City's internal work under the city information security policy. Services must not use user input for training, or must have that function disabled; staff need prior approval of their head of division, may not input personal or other confidential or not-yet-public information, may not use answers unchecked, must have outputs checked by several staff before use in documents, and must state that external documents were created with generative AI.

instruments.english_title: Sapporo City Generative AI Compliance Rules (AI-HR002)
instruments.issuing_authority: Sapporo City, Director-General of the Digital Strategy Promotion Bureau (デジタル戦略推進局長決裁)
instruments.current_status: Made 28 December 2023; amended 26 February 2025 (in force 1 March 2025), 2 May 2025, 1 September 2025, 31 March 2026 (in force 1 April 2026) and 15 June 2026 (latest amendment, in force the same day). Standard rule AI-HR002 of the Sapporo generative AI usage guideline group.
instruments.summary: Binding internal rules for Sapporo City staff using generative AI. Use must be notified in advance to the head of the Administrative Reform and DX Promotion Office, who may comment; staff must respect copyright and other rights and check legality, limit external generative AI to confidentiality-class-1 information, never handle non-disclosable information under Art. 7 of the city information disclosure ordinance, not let non-staff use the city's generative AI directly, and review and correct all outputs. The office head may grant exceptions allowing information up to confidentiality class 3B where inputs are not used for training, or direct use by non-staff where the risk is judged acceptable.

instruments.current_status: Decided 26 February 2025 by the Director-General of the Digital Strategy Promotion Bureau; in force 1 March 2025 (附則). Standard rule AI-HR001 of the Sapporo generative AI usage guideline group.
instruments.summary: One-page policy setting Sapporo City's basic approach to using generative AI in its work, as a standard rule of the city's generative AI usage guideline group (with practical rules in a separate handbook). The city commits to actively using generative AI, including trials, starting with internal administration and extending to common and individual business areas, to examining better uses over the medium to long term, and to raising staff knowledge and skills, using its Digital CoE framework across bureaus.

instruments.summary: Guideline of the Sendai City Board of Education applying to all Sendai municipal schools and the board itself, setting basic principles and phased stages for using generative AI in school administration and in classes. It sets operating standards and checklists for staff and teachers: follow providers' latest terms (age limits, parental consent, permitted educational use), do not enter personal information such as names or photos into prompts, verify outputs, and guide pupils in information ethics and AI literacy; it does not uniformly ban or mandate use.

organizations.name: National Diet
organizations.ai_governance_role: Enacts Acts, including the Road Traffic Act and Road Transport Vehicle Act provisions on automated driving systems.

organizations.name: Cabinet
organizations.ai_governance_role: Makes Cabinet Orders under the AI Promotion Act (Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters Order) and adopts the Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan by Cabinet decision (Art. 18 AI Promotion Act).

organizations.name: Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters
organizations.ai_governance_role: Cabinet-level headquarters established under Chapter 4 of the AI Promotion Act (in operation from 1 September 2025), headed by the Prime Minister with all Ministers of State as members; drafts the AI Basic Plan and decided the Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (19 December 2025).

organizations.name: Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council
organizations.ai_governance_role: Ministerial council (chaired by the Chief Cabinet Secretary) that decided the Social Principles of Human-Centric AI (2019) and AI Strategy 2019, 2021 and 2022.

organizations.name: AI Strategy Council
organizations.ai_governance_role: Expert council on AI strategy (2023-2025) under the Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council; issued the Tentative Summary of AI Issues (2023) and, with its AI Institutional Study Group, the Interim Report (2025) that led to the AI Promotion Act.

organizations.name: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
organizations.ai_governance_role: Co-issues the AI Guidelines for Business with METI (through the Conference toward AI Network Society); issued the 2017 Draft AI R&D Guidelines and 2019 AI Utilization Guidelines; issues AI security technical guidelines and the AI guidebook for local governments.

organizations.name: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry
organizations.ai_governance_role: Co-issues the AI Guidelines for Business with MIC (secretariat of the AI Business Guidelines study group, jointly with IPA/AISI from its 4th meeting); issues AI contract guidance, the 2021-22 Governance Guidelines for Implementation of AI Principles and guidance on civil liability and generative AI in content production.

organizations.name: Digital Agency
organizations.ai_governance_role: Secretariat of the Council for the Promotion of a Digital Society and its Executive Committee; publishes the Digital Society Promotion Standard Guidelines, including DS-920 on government procurement and use of generative AI, and related generative-AI notices for ministries.

organizations.name: Japan AI Safety Institute
organizations.ai_governance_role: Japan's AI Safety Institute (AISI, housed in the Information-technology Promotion Agency); publishes AI safety evaluation, red-teaming, data-quality and AI-governance guides.

organizations.name: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issues guidance on generative AI use in primary and secondary schools.

organizations.name: Personal Information Protection Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Independent data protection authority (個人情報保護委員会) administering the APPI; issued the June 2023 generative-AI alert and the 2025 DeepSeek notice, ran the 3-year review and drafted the 2026 APPI amendment bill; now preparing implementing Cabinet Orders, PPC rules and guidelines.

organizations.name: Agency for Cultural Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Copyright authority (文化庁, Copyright Division) and secretariat of the Council for Cultural Affairs Copyright Subdivision; publishes official interpretations of Copyright Act Art. 30-4 and the 2024 'General Understanding on AI and Copyright' and AI-copyright checklist.

organizations.name: Intellectual Property Strategy Headquarters
organizations.ai_governance_role: Cabinet IP strategy body (知的財産戦略本部) with its Cabinet Office secretariat (内閣府知的財産戦略推進事務局); hosts the AI Era Intellectual Property Rights Study Group, which produced the 2024 interim summary and the 2026 Principle Code on IP protection and transparency for generative AI.

organizations.name: Japan Patent Office
organizations.ai_governance_role: Patent authority (特許庁, METI); publishes examination case examples on AI-related inventions in the Patent and Utility Model Examination Handbook.

organizations.name: Financial Services Agency
organizations.ai_governance_role: Integrated financial regulator; issued the AI Discussion Paper (v1.0 2025, v1.1 2026), ran the FSA AI Public-Private Forum (2025) and the Principles for Model Risk Management (2021) covering AI/ML models.

organizations.name: Ministry of Defense
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issued the MOD Basic Policy on the Promotion of AI Utilization (2024) and the Guidelines for Responsible AI Application in R&D of Defense Equipment (2025).

organizations.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
organizations.ai_governance_role: Regulates medical devices including AI-based software (change-plan confirmation scheme for AI medical devices under the PMD Act Enforcement Regulations), issues notices on AI in clinical practice and medical-data use for AI R&D.

organizations.name: Ministry of Justice
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issues guidance on how AI legal-services tools relate to the Attorney Act Article 72 ban on unlicensed legal practice (2023, 2026).

organizations.name: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism
organizations.ai_governance_role: Vehicle safety regulator: safety standards for automated driving systems (自動運行装置) under the Road Transport Vehicle Act and safety guidelines for automated vehicles.

organizations.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Digital Services
organizations.ai_governance_role: Tokyo Metropolitan Government bureau responsible for digital policy; issued the Tokyo AI Strategy (2025), the AI Introduction and Utilization Guideline and the generative AI usage handbook for staff (2026).

organizations.name: Kobe City
organizations.ai_governance_role: Designated city in Hyogo Prefecture; enacted Japan's first comprehensive municipal AI ordinance (2024), its basic AI policy and staff generative AI guidelines, administered by the Digital Strategy Department of the Planning and Coordination Bureau.

organizations.name: Osaka City Digital Integration Office
organizations.ai_governance_role: Designated city; its Digital Integration Office (デジタル統括室) issues the city's generative AI usage guideline for staff, the companion guideline for contractors and designated managers, and the AI governance advisor scheme.

organizations.name: Aichi Prefecture
organizations.ai_governance_role: Prefectural government; its Digital Strategy Division and Chief AI Officer (デジタル戦略監) run the prefecture's generative AI procurement and use guideline (2026).

organizations.name: Hyogo Prefecture
organizations.ai_governance_role: Prefectural government; its Digital Strategy Division issues the Hyogo generative AI usage guideline for staff (first version October 2023) and ran the ChatGPT and generative AI utilisation project team.

organizations.name: Chiba Prefecture
organizations.ai_governance_role: Prefectural government; its Digital Reform Promotion Bureau and Digital Promotion Division issue the prefecture's staff generative AI usage guideline (first version June 2023) and designate the generative AI services staff may use.

organizations.name: Chiba City
organizations.ai_governance_role: Designated city; its General Affairs Bureau Information Management Department issued the city's guideline on the use of ChatGPT and other generative AI (2023).

organizations.name: Sapporo City
organizations.ai_governance_role: Designated city; its Digital Strategy Promotion Bureau and Administrative Reform and DX Promotion Office run the 'Sapporo generative AI usage guideline group', including the generative AI utilisation policy and compliance rules for staff.

organizations.name: Sendai City Board of Education
organizations.ai_governance_role: Board of education of the designated city of Sendai; issued the Sendai generative AI utilisation guideline for municipal schools (Ver.1, revised as Ver.2 in May 2025).
